title: cohort-forwarding-and-safety-for-hybrid-version-pin-rollouts
creator: Michael Chen
description: Problem: We need a deterministic, low-risk way to roll out model version pins across geo/region/tier routing policies while preserving session stickiness, enabling safe rapid rollback, and avoiding user-visible flapping when fallback variants are exercised. Current route resolver supports basic version affinity and TTL-driven pins but lacks: (1) a coherent cohort-forwarding model for when a session's pinned variant becomes unavailable in a region/tier, (2) explicit rollback isolation so canary failures don't cascade to healthy cohorts, and (3) a small-signal gating mechanism tied to fine-grained metrics for automated rollback decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Add cohort-forwarding semantics: when a pinned variant is unreachable for a request, the resolver should attempt forward routing to a configured ordered list (local fallback variant -> same-region alternate -> global fallback) while preserving a per-session pin TTL and recording forwarding events for evaluation.

Implement a rollback-safety envelope: canary cohorts must be independently isolatable such that a rollback of a canary variant does not reassign or invalidate pins for control cohorts; session pins should optionally decay to a neutral state rather than force immediate remapping.

Expose a metric gating API: rollout controller can declare threshold rules (latency P95, error-rate, quality-regression) that will automatically pause/escalate rollouts and emit detailed diffs to the rollout dashboard.
Add unit and integration tests for: pin expiry, forwarding ordering, probabilistic cohort split (A/B percentages), forced rollback, and simultaneous multi-region failover.
Rollout in staged experiment to 1%/5%/20% cohorts with synthetic traffic and alerting; no regression in platform P99 latency beyond 5% of baseline.
Instrument forwarding events, variant fallback counts, and cohort-level quality deltas in Console. Dashboard and alert runbook links included in PR.
New routing config is backwards-compatible: existing routing rules continue to work without agent-side changes unless the new flags are enabled.
Performance: resolver decision path should add <1ms median latency in the common case and not increase CPU by more than 3% under production traffic profiles.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Michael Chen: Initial scoping done. Spent time mapping existing resolver code paths and identified two hot spots: (a) session-pin lookup and (b) variant availability checks that perform a synchronous region capability query. Proposal: cache variant availability for 30s with invalidation on capacity events.
